actions.action: Unpot the plant and remove most of the old moisture-retaining medium from the roots
Soak the roots for 15 minutes in 200 ml water with one drop of methylene blue
Soak coconut coir crumbs for 15 minutes, then squeeze out the excess water
Mix the coir evenly with pine bark for aeration
Replant in a pot with plenty of drainage holes, centering the plant and spreading the medium around the roots
After a few days, water slowly and evenly with 1/2 liter of water containing one dissolved vitamin B1 tablet
Place the plant in a cool, well-ventilated spot with diffused light
From about day 15, water weekly with fresh strained rice water (3 tbsp rice in 1/2 liter water)

verdict.reason: The answer blames old, moisture-retaining medium and repots into an airy coir/bark mix in a well-draining pot, which matches the fix, but it never names overwatering, so the diagnosis is partial; the extras (methylene blue, B1, rice water) are unnecessary but not likely harmful.
